from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["RNNs struggle with long sentences.", "Attention focuses on relevant information.", "Like finding clues in a mystery."]
        self.setup_layout("The Problem: Information Overload", lecture_lines)
        
        # Hide lecture lines for sequential reveal if needed
        for line in self.lecture:
            line.set_opacity(0)
            
        # Animation
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        rnn_text = Text("RNN", color=BLUE).scale(1.2)
        sequence_text = Text("Sequence", color=WHITE).scale(1.2)
        dots = Text("...", color=WHITE)
        
        group = VGroup(rnn_text, dots, sequence_text).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(group, "C3")
        
        self.play(Write(rnn_text), Write(sequence_text), FadeIn(dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(dots.animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        
        magnifying_glass = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW).add(Text("Q", color=YELLOW).scale(0.8))
        self.place_at_grid(magnifying_glass, "C3")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(rnn_text),
            FadeOut(sequence_text),
            ReplacementTransform(dots, magnifying_glass)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Query asks what I need.", "Key acts as a label.", "Value provides the actual content."]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Components: Q, K, and V", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define assets
        q_box = Square(color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=0.5)
        k_box = Square(color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.5)
        v_box = Square(color="#3357FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        q_label = Text("Q", font_size=24, color="#FF5733").next_to(q_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        k_label = Text("K", font_size=24, color="#33FF57").next_to(k_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        v_label = Text("V", font_size=24, color="#3357FF").next_to(v_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Magnifying glass
        magnifier = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE).add(Text("🔍", font_size=20))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(q_box, q_label), "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(k_box, k_label), "B4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(v_box, v_label), "B6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(VGroup(q_box, q_label, k_box, k_label, v_box, v_label)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_at_grid(magnifier, "B4")
        self.play(Create(magnifier))
        self.play(magnifier.animate.shift(0.5*DOWN), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        v_final = v_box.copy().set_fill(opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(v_final, "E4")
        self.play(Transform(v_box.copy(), v_final))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Calculating Relevance: Dot Product & Softmax", [
            "Dot product measures item similarity.",
            "Softmax converts scores into probabilities.",
            "High scores highlight relevant words."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Dot product grid
        grid_data = [[8.5, 1.2, 0.5], [0.8, 7.2, 0.4], [0.3, 0.6, 9.1]]
        matrix = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            row = VGroup()
            for j in range(3):
                val = DecimalNumber(grid_data[i][j], num_decimal_places=1, font_size=30)
                box = Square(side_length=0.7, color=WHITE).add(val)
                row.add(box)
            matrix.add(row.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0))
        matrix.arrange(DOWN, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(matrix, "A2", "C4")
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Softmax visualization (labels)
        softmax_label = Text("Softmax", font_size=24, color="#FF00FF")

        self.play(Write(softmax_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Bringing it Together: Scaled Dot-Product Attention", 
                          ["Weights multiply the input Values.", "This creates a weighted sum.", "Result is the understood representation."])
        
        # Define colors consistent with semantic roles
        weight_color = YELLOW
        value_color = BLUE
        result_color = GREEN

        # Initial Setup (Assets/Mobjects)
        weights = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=weight_color, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(3)])
        values = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=value_color, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(3)])
        
        # Positioning
        for i, w in enumerate(weights):
            self.place_at_grid(w, f"B{i+2}")
        for i, v in enumerate(values):
            self.place_at_grid(v, f"D{i+2}")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(weight_color))
        self.play(FadeIn(weights), FadeIn(values))
        
        lines = VGroup(*[Line(weights[i].get_bottom(), values[i].get_top(), color=WHITE) for i in range(3)])
        self.play(Create(lines))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(value_color))
        weighted_sum_label = Text("Weighted Sum", font_size=20, color=result_color)
        self.place_at_grid(weighted_sum_label, "E3")
        self.play(FadeIn(weighted_sum_label))
        
        # Show combination
        arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(lines[i].get_end(), weighted_sum_label.get_top(), color=result_color, buff=0.1) for i in range(3)])
        self.play(Create(arrows))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(result_color))
        final_vector = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=1.0, color=result_color, fill_opacity=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(final_vector, "F4")
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(VGroup(weights, values, lines, arrows, weighted_sum_label), final_vector))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Multi-head attention runs in parallel.", "Capture different relationship types.", "Synthesize into one final summary."]
        self.setup_layout("Application: Multi-Head Attention", lecture_lines)
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0)
        
        # Color constants
        c_grammar = GREEN
        c_sentiment = BLUE
        c_logic = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        
        # Three attention modules
        module1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, height=1.5, width=1.0, color=c_grammar).set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        module2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, height=1.5, width=1.0, color=c_sentiment).set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        module3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, height=1.5, width=1.0, color=c_logic).set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        
        modules = VGroup(module1, module2, module3).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(modules, "B3", "E5")
        self.play(Create(modules))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # Connections
        conn1 = Line(module1.get_top(), module1.get_bottom(), color=c_grammar)
        conn2 = Line(module2.get_top(), module2.get_bottom(), color=c_sentiment)
        conn3 = Line(module3.get_top(), module3.get_bottom(), color=c_logic)
        
        self.play(Create(conn1), Create(conn2), Create(conn3))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        
        output_box = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=3.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(opacity=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(output_box, "F4")
        
        arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(m.get_bottom(), output_box.get_top(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1) for m in [module1, module2, module3]])
        
        self.play(Create(output_box), Create(arrows))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming/linear algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Problem: Information Overload
sections.content: Introduce the limitation of previous models (RNNs) which struggle with long-range dependencies. Define 'Attention' as the ability to selectively focus on relevant parts of input.
sections.example: Reading a long mystery novel: You don't memorize every word; you focus on the clues that link the detective to the culprit.

sections.title: The Core Components: Query, Key, and Value
sections.content: Explain the Q, K, V retrieval system using an analogy to a library database. Visual: Query (what I want), Key (the labels on the book spines), Value (the content inside).
sections.example: A library search: Your search term (Query) is compared against book titles (Keys) to retrieve the most useful information (Values).

sections.title: Calculating Relevance: Dot Product & Softmax
sections.content: Introduce the mathematical intuition: Score = (Query · Key) / sqrt(d). Use a heat map graphic to show how similar items get higher weights, then 'Softmax' turns these into probabilities (percentages).
sections.example: Visualizing a 'focus matrix': If the word is 'Apple', the matrix shows a bright 'red' spot on 'fruit' and a 'dim' spot on 'jump'.

sections.title: Bringing it Together: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
sections.content: Combine the concepts: Multiply the weights by the Values to get a 'weighted sum.' This is the final vector representation that the model 'understands'.
sections.example: Imagine a chef choosing ingredients: The weight (Attention) determines how much salt or spice (Value) goes into the final dish based on the recipe (Query).

sections.title: Application: Multi-Head Attention
sections.content: Explain that Transformers run multiple 'attention' processes in parallel to capture different types of relationships simultaneously (grammar, sentiment, context).
sections.example: A team of researchers: One person focuses on the historical facts, another on the emotional tone, and a third on the scientific logic—all synthesizing one final summary.
